pages.text: $(l)Diode$()$(br)Passes power $(item)one way only$(), from its back to its front, without changing the voltage. Use it to feed a network that must never send power back.

$(l)Potentiometer$()$(br)A bridge with a dial: it passes from $(item)0 to 100%$() of its input voltage, 100% by default. It is also a $(item)display link$() source for voltage.$(br2)Right-click a diode or a potentiometer with $(item)heavy machinery casing$() to encase it.

$(l)Resistor$()$(br)A plain $(item)consumer$() with a fixed resistance. It connects on its back face and turns power into nothing, which makes it a handy test load to check that your generators keep up.

Wind it on the $(item)winding machine$() with a $(item)constantan spool$(). The dial sets its resistance in steps of 10 ohms, up to $(item)1,000 ohms$(). Remember that a lower resistance draws more: at 300 V, 100 ohms use 900 W, 1,000 ohms only 90 W.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
